question: A finance team is designing a way of working in which Claude prepares the monthly variance commentary. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Write the instruction for the rest; try it on last month's figures; decide which parts a person must own; adjust one thing and try again
B) Try it on last month's figures; decide which parts a person must own; write the instruction for the rest; adjust one thing and try again
C) Decide which parts a person must own; write the instruction for the rest; try it on last month's figures; adjust one thing and try again
D) Write the instruction for the rest; decide which parts a person must own; adjust one thing and try again; try it on last month's figures
correct_answers: C) Decide which parts a person must own; write the instruction for the rest; try it on last month's figures; adjust one thing and try again
explanations: Writing instructions before deciding what stays human means the instruction may quietly cover work that should never have been handed over.
Testing before the boundary or the instruction exists gives a result nobody can interpret, and the design decisions come too late to shape it.
Correct. Delegation boundaries come first: decide what a person must own, write instructions for the remainder, test on real past figures, then adjust one thing at a time.
Adjusting before the arrangement has been tried at all means the first adjustment is made blind, and the test arrives after the changes.
